2607.06258.title: Early Language Learning via Spreading Activation and Category Exploration in Complex Networks
2607.06258.paper_summary: Is word acquisition in children uneven with respect to semantic and lexical categories? To answer this question, we model early language learning as a search on a graph-based mental lexicon, driven by two interacting processes: spreading activation and an enforced exploration (rather than exploitation) of lexical categories. We evaluate model performance on four languages (German, English, Dutch, and Rioplatense Spanish), using CDIs as ground-truth data for lexical categories, normative ages derived from the Wordbank repository, and state-of-the-art resources for reconstructing graphs of word similarities. We find that spreading activation outperforms a shortest path baseline in simulating normative word acquisition. At the category level, we highlight complex transitions between CDIs. By studying their sequences in terms of burstiness and average persistence time within the same CDI, we find that spreading activation better captures the exploration dynamics observed empirically. Overall, our findings suggest that vocabulary development can be understood through the non-trivial interplay between activation dynamics and some degree of constraints regulating the visiting of lexical categories in complex networks.
2607.06258.paper_summary_zh: 兒童的詞彙獲取在語義和詞彙類別上是否不均衡？為了回答這個問題，我們將早期語言學習建模為在基於圖的心理詞彙上的搜索，這一過程由兩個相互作用的過程驅動：擴散激活和對詞彙類別的強制探索（而非利用）。我們在四種語言（德語、英語、荷蘭語和里奧普拉滕西西班牙語）上評估模型性能，使用CDI作為詞彙類別的真實數據，從Wordbank資料庫導出的標準年齡，以及用於重建單詞相似度圖的最先進資源。我們發現擴散激活在模擬標準詞彙獲取方面優於最短路徑基準。在類別層面上，我們突出了CDI之間的複雜過渡。通過研究它們在同一CDI內的序列，從突發性和平均持續時間的角度，我們發現擴散激活更好地捕捉到實證觀察到的探索動態。總的來說，我們的研究結果表明，詞彙發展可以通過激活動態與某種程度的約束在複雜網絡中調節詞彙類別訪問之間的非平凡相互作用來理解。
2607.06258.author: Salvatore Citraro et.al.
